content_units: End-of-Term Documentary Picks for Ages 11–14
These 10 documentaries are broadly suitable for middle-school viewers, stay under 100 minutes, and lean toward science, nature, engineering, or uplifting real-world stories.
Classroom-Friendly Recommendation Table
Title   Runtime   Topic   Age Fit   Why it works for ages 11–14   Classroom discussion question

Wings of Life   (2011)   81 min   Nature / pollination   11–14   Visually engaging, clear science connections, gentle tone   How do tiny pollinators make a big difference in human life and ecosystems?

Jane   (2017)   90 min   Nature / animal behavior / science   12–14   Inspiring scientist role model, rich wildlife footage, thoughtful but accessible   What helped Jane Goodall challenge expectations and make new discoveries?

Bears   (2014)   78 min   Nature / ecosystems / survival   11–13   Family-friendly wildlife story with strong visuals and low complexity   How does storytelling help us care more about animals and habitats?

March of the Penguins   (2005)   80 min   Nature / adaptation / survival   11–14   Familiar, emotionally engaging, excellent for adaptation and environment themes   Which penguin adaptations are most important for survival, and why?

Apollo 11   (2019)   93 min   Space / engineering / history   12–14   Exciting archival footage, strong STEM links, inspiring teamwork   What kinds of planning and engineering made the moon landing possible?

Dream Big: Engineering Our World   (2017)   42 min   Engineering / design / problem-solving   11–14   Short, upbeat, highly classroom-friendly, showcases real engineers   Which engineering problem in your community would you most want to solve?

The Short Game   (2013)   99 min   Human stories / discipline / growth   11–14   Focuses on effort, pressure, and perseverance without heavy content   How can competition help people grow, and when can it become unhealthy?

Spellbound   (2002)   97 min   Human stories / learning / perseverance   11–14   Inspiring students, relatable academic pressure, diverse backgrounds   What matters more for success: talent, practice, support, or confidence?

Pick of the Litter   (2018)   81 min   Human-animal teamwork / perseverance   11–14   Warm, motivating, easy to follow, strong themes of resilience and service   What qualities make a dog—and a person—well suited for helping others?

Science Fair   (2018)   90 min   Science / innovation / student achievement   11–14   Student-centered, funny and motivating, ideal for school audiences   What makes a strong scientific question, and how do setbacks improve research?
Best Fits for a Reward-Day Screening
Option 1:   Dream Big: Engineering Our World     Short, energetic STEM pick with broad appeal   Best for mixed-attention groups
Learn more
Option 2:   Apollo 11     High-interest space documentary with real engineering depth   Best for older middle schoolers
Learn more
Option 3:   Science Fair     Student-focused and inspiring without feeling too academic   Best for end-of-term motivation
Learn more
Option 4:   Wings of Life     Calm, beautiful, and easy to pair with life-science discussion   Best for broad age fit
Learn more
Selection Notes for Your Class
- Age fit assumes typical school viewing with teacher supervision.
- I prioritized titles with minimal graphic material and low political intensity.
- A few films include emotional moments or mild tension, but none are known primarily for disturbing content.
